title: Finite scheme quotient of an admissible tame action
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$ by scheme automorphisms. Suppose $X$ has a cover by $G$-invariant affine opens and the action is tame: for every geometric point $\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the order of $\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$ is invertible in its residue field. Then there is a scheme $Y$ and an invariant morphism $q:X\to Y$ which is finite surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with geometric fibres the $G$-orbits, quotient topology on $|Y|$, and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian. Every $G$-invariant morphism from $X$ to any scheme factors uniquely through $q$. For each invariant affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the cover, $q(U)$ is open, $q^{-1}q(U)=U$, and the restricted quotient is $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}(R^G)$, where $R^G=\{r\in R:g(r)=r\text{ for all }g\in G\}$. No logarithmic structure, generic freeness, integrality, excellence or finite-type base is assumed. Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

proof.text: Every orbit is contained in one of the given invariant affine opens: choose one containing any point of the orbit, and invariance contains the rest. Thus [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts] applies to $X,G$. It gives an invariant affine integral surjection $q:X\to Y$, the orbit-space topology, geometric orbit fibres, and the categorical universal property for arbitrary scheme targets. Its invariant-section description on every affine open of $Y$ gives $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$: the canonical map has this image on an affine basis, and sections and invariant sections both glue uniquely. Retain the invariant affine chart cover $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ with $V_j=q(W_j)=\operatorname{Spec}(R_j^G)$ supplied by that node.

source.place: Expose VI 3.2, printed p.74, and 3.7(b), printed p.75; agent expansion of the underlying scheme-quotient input.

proof.text: Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be any affine open of $Y$. The affine quotient theorem identifies $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and identifies $A$ with $R^G$. This source is an affine open of the locally Noetherian scheme $X$, so [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $R$ Noetherian. The $G$-action restricts to this open, since $q$ is invariant. For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, choose an algebraic closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; its residue embedding defines a geometric point over $\mathfrak p$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [def-weil-geometric-point] its residue-field map into the algebraically closed field is injective. Therefore $g$ fixes this geometric point if and only if it fixes $\mathfrak p$ and acts identically on $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; this is precisely $I_{\mathfrak p}$ in [lem-per-tame-inertia-surjective-group-trace]. The assumed tame geometric stabilizers therefore verify that lemma's hypotheses, giving $a\in R$ with $\sum_g g(a)=1$. This applies to every affine $V$, including the $V_j$ of step 1.

source.place: Expose VI 3.2, printed p.74, and 3.7(b), printed p.75; agent expansion of the underlying scheme-quotient input.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-trace-one-noetherian-invariant-finiteness] to each ring $R$ from step 2, with the same finite group and its trace-one element. It gives that $A=R^G$ is Noetherian and $R$ is a finite $A$-module. Since this holds for every affine open $V$ of $Y$, and $q$ is affine by step 1, the definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] says exactly that $q$ is finite. Its surjectivity was already supplied in step 1.

source.place: Expose VI 3.2, printed p.74, and 3.7(b), printed p.75; agent expansion of the underlying scheme-quotient input.

proof.text: The $V_j$ from step 1 are an affine open cover with Noetherian coordinate rings by step 3; hence $Y$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. It is quasi-compact by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]: pull an arbitrary open cover of $Y$ back along $q$; quasi-compactness of $X$ gives finitely many inverse images covering $X$, and surjectivity implies the corresponding finitely many opens cover $Y$. Consequently $Y$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Expose VI 3.2, printed p.74, and 3.7(b), printed p.75; agent expansion of the underlying scheme-quotient input.

proof.text: Now fix any invariant affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the cover in the statement, not just one of the auxiliary $W_j$. Every orbit meeting $U$ is contained in $U$, so the orbit fibres give $q^{-1}q(U)=U$. The quotient topology makes $q(U)$ open, and [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts] identifies $U\to q(U)$ as its categorical quotient. The restriction is finite: for every affine open of $q(U)$ the very same ring map was tested for finiteness in step 3 [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. It is surjective, with affine source $U$. The open subscheme $q(U)$ of Noetherian $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-affine-target-noetherian] applies and makes $q(U)$ affine. Applying the invariant-section clause of [lem-per-admissible-quotient-affine-integral-charts] to this affine open identifies its coordinate ring with $R^G$, and the map on sections with the inclusion $R^G\hookrightarrow R$. By the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the restricted morphism is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}(R^G)$, as required. All inputs used only the stated Noetherianity, invariant affine cover and tame stabilizers.
